The results for $c\ge1$ and the $\limsup$, as well as the limits and the inverse theorem for $q\in\{2,3\}$, have been formalized and machine-checked in the Lean~4 proof assistant.
comments: 16 pages, 1 figure, Lean verification

title: Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4
abstract: For a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d\ge 2$ with $p(0)=0$ and $p'(0)\ne 0$, let $S(p)$ be the minimum of $|p(c)/(c\,p'(0))|$ over the critical points $c$ of $p$, and let $K(d)$ be the supremum of $S(p)$ over all such $p$ of degree $d$. In 1981 Smale proved that $K(d)\le 4$ for every $d$, and asked whether $4$ can be replaced by $1$. We prove that Smale's mean value constant $\sup_dK(d)$ equals $4$ and that $K(d)\to4$ as $d\to\infty$, combining a reduction due to Jatar and Ng with an explicit construction. In particular, $4$ cannot be replaced by any smaller constant. Each $K(d)$ is known to be below $4$, so the supremum is not attained. The main result has also been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
comments: 11 pages, 3 figures. A Lean 4 proof of the main theorem: https://github.com/david44hello/paper_smale-mean-value-constant-equals-4/tree/v2.50 . An expanded version, with further results: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24069916

title: The four-dimensional Borsuk number is five or six
abstract: Can every set of diameter one in four dimensions be split into at most five parts of smaller diameter? Three parts suffice in the plane and four in three-dimensional space. In four dimensions five parts are sometimes necessary. We prove that six always suffice, improving the previous upper bound of seven. For small circumradius we use six cones. For large circumradius five balls meet every diametral pair of a compact set. At intermediate radii we bound the diameter of each part by the diameter of a rational polytope. The theorem is formalised in Lean.
comments: The main theorem is formalised in Lean 4 using only the standard axioms of propositional extensionality, classical choice, and quotient soundness. Available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23966881

title: The Ulam sequence grows subexponentially
abstract: We prove that the $n$-th element of the Ulam sequence, a somewhat mysterious recursively-defined sequence of positive integers, has size $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$; previous upper bounds were exponential in $n$. Our argument uses an additive-combinatorial lemma, possibly of independent interest, about covering finite difference sets with multiplicatively short intervals. The proofs are due to ChatGPT.

title: Agent-written heuristics versus commercial solvers on unsolved job-shop benchmark instances
abstract: Commercial solvers are the standard tool for difficult scheduling problems. We study whether a frontier large language model, used as a coding agent with open-source tools only, can match them in quality and speed. We report every run, and independent checkers verify every schedule. On the 100,000-operation job shop tai_100_1000_1, an agent-written solver reached 525,515, below OptalCP, Hexaly, and CP Optimizer. Unchanged, it improved all ten instances of the family and closed two. With equal budgets on the same workstation, it ended 0.0-1.8% above the lower bound, against 2.6-5.8% for CP Optimizer and 2.4-4.4% for Hexaly. On the Behnke-Geiger flexible job shops, an agent-written tabu search improved 11 of 32 open instances. With two transport robots, an agent-written solver improved seven of ten MKT instances. New lower bounds show that four published MKT values cannot be attained on the distributed instance files. Agent-run improvement campaigns closed eight further instances.
comments: 27 pages, 4 figures, 14 tables. Submitted to International Transactions in Operational Research. Data, schedules, checkers and code: https://github.com/andrealbrechtl/agent-heuristics-jobshop-supplement/

title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
abstract: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$. In the present paper, the non-negligible assumption is removed using a rigidity criterion developed previously by the author for use in non-semisimple categories. We also present a variant result (found without further AI assistance) that $X$ is also rigid if $\dim\mathrm{Hom}((DX)^{\otimes n}\otimes X^{\otimes n},\mathbf{1})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, where $D$ is the Grothendieck-Verdier duality functor of $\mathcal{C}$. Using this variant, we show that if $V$ is a simple self-contragredient vertex operator algebra such that the category $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ of $C_1$-cofinite grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is closed under contragredient modules, then $\mathcal{C}^1_V$ is a locally finite $\mathbb{C}$-linear abelian rigid braided ribbon category. We also show that if $V$ is a simple $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded self-contragredient $C_2$-cofinite vertex operator algebra, then the category of all grading-restricted generalized $V$-modules is a (not necessarily semisimple) modular tensor category.
comments: 29 pages

title: The Polyak-Łojasiewicz Paper: A 10-Year Retrospective
abstract: In 2016, we wrote a paper introducing the phrase "Polyak-Lojasiewicz (PL) condition" for an old idea, unsure of how readers would react. The paper ultimately had a larger impact than we expected, and we are surprised and honoured to receive the 2026 PKDD ECML Test of Time Award. With 10 years of hindsight, this note offers an informal and candid retrospective on the PL condition. We take a look back at the origins of the paper, give an AI-assisted refined version of the main theorem, review criticisms of the work, and discuss a variety of related ideas and extensions.
comments: 20 pages, 6 figures

title: HOL in HOL: mechanized soundness, completeness and consistency, with and without infinity
abstract: What can a logic certify about a copy of itself? For Church's simple theory of types, formalized as a deep embedding in Isabelle/HOL with Henkin semantics and a natural-deduction calculus, the answer has two tiers. On the first tier, plain Isabelle/HOL certifies the logic without an axiom of infinity, by a standard model with one individual. On the second tier, the logic with a Dedekind-style axiom of infinity is certified only in Isabelle/HOL extended by a large enough set-theoretic universe. Both tiers appear in Harrison's self-verification of HOL Light. What the present formalization adds is Henkin completeness, and with it a semantics that matches the calculus exactly, compactness and model existence on the first tier, and the boundary between the tiers. Comparing two ways of adding infinity to the object logic shows where the boundary lies. One is an infinite domain of individuals, expressed by the first-order sentences "there are at least $n$ individuals", each of which has a finite model; the other is the Dedekind axiom, a single sentence with no finite model, and there the first tier ends. In the calculus the axiom is strictly stronger than the sentences together: it derives each of them, but they do not derive it. The witness is a countable Henkin model in which every sentence holds and the axiom fails, because its function domain is too sparse for an injective, non-surjective self-map. On the second tier, the universe serves one purpose only: to prove the Dedekind axiom consistent. Everything that follows, completeness and even the countable Henkin model of the axiom, is obtained in plain Isabelle/HOL. The universe axiom is Harrison-style, realized in Paulson's ZFC_in_HOL with the domain of every type in $V_{ω+ω}$; with it, full classical higher-order logic with infinity and relational choice is consistent relative to set theory.
comments: 23 pages, 1 figure. Formal proof artifacts: Archive of Formal Proofs entries HOL_in_HOL_Deep and HOL_in_HOL_Deep_Infinity_ZFC (Isabelle2026). Submitted

title: Goodman-type lower bounds for graph homomorphism densities
abstract: For a finite graph $H$ with $v(H)$ vertices, chromatic number $χ(H)$, and chromatic polynomial $P_H$, define $Φ_H(p)=(1-p)^{v(H)}P_H((1-p)^{-1})$. This polynomial interpolates the homomorphism densities of $H$ in balanced complete multipartite graphons. We study the lower bound $t(H,W)\geΦ_H(p)$ on the homomorphism density of $H$ in graphons $W$ of edge density $p>1-1/(χ(H)-1)$, which generalises Goodman's triangle bound. We prove the inequality for chordal graphs whose maximal cliques have equal size, for trivially perfect graphs, and for joins of a clique and an odd cycle. The proofs use entropy along clique trees and a convexity criterion for adding a universal vertex. We also prove that a nonbipartite graph satisfies the inequality at all sufficiently high edge densities if and only if its girth is odd. For a graph on $n$ vertices whose girth is odd, the bound holds whenever $p>1-(72n^{12})^{-1}$. The proof combines Whitney's forest expansion with a spectral comparison of cycle densities. Finally, among the $117$ nonbipartite graphs on at most six vertices with no isolated vertices or isolated edges, exactly $94$ satisfy the bound. The main results are formally verified in Lean 4.
comments: 35 pages, 2 figures, 1 table

title: Muon Attains $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ Iteration Complexity under Shuffling
abstract: Muon is a stochastic first-order optimizer for matrix-valued parameters. It maintains an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients in a momentum buffer with coefficient $β$, and orthogonalizes the buffer to obtain the update direction. Muon has been reported to accelerate and stabilize the training of large language models. In practice, it is often used with shuffling (sampling without replacement), where each epoch visits the components of a finite-sum objective in a permuted order. However, its iteration complexity in this setting remains open. We analyze Muon under shuffling, with the momentum buffer orthogonalized by the polar map. For smooth nonconvex finite-sum problems, we establish an $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3})$ iteration complexity for finding an $\varepsilon$-stationary point. This guarantee holds for every sequence of permutations, covering random reshuffling, shuffle once, and the incremental gradient method. This complexity matches that of stochastic gradient descent under shuffling in its dependence on $\varepsilon$, and improves on Muon's $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ complexity under sampling with replacement. Our guarantee requires a problem-dependent $β$ that approaches one as the number of components grows. In contrast, no fixed $β$ guarantees convergence to stationarity for every number of components. We show this by constructing a family of smooth convex problems on which, for any fixed $β\in[0,1)$, Muon remains bounded away from stationarity once the number of components is sufficiently large. This failure occurs for every sequence of permutations and persists even with small stepsizes. These results suggest two practical tuning rules: if the training loss stops decreasing even after reducing the stepsize, increase $β$; when increasing $β$, reduce the stepsize accordingly.
comments: 25 pages, 14 figures

title: The Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth
abstract: We determine the Benjamin-Feir stability diagram for small-amplitude Stokes waves with constant vorticity in finite depth. For the full water wave system, we derive an explicit instability index and rigorously classify its sign throughout the depth-vorticity plane. With gravitational acceleration and carrier wavenumber normalized to one, we identify a unique minimum depth $h_{\text{crit}}\approx1.36271$, below which Benjamin-Feir instability is absent for every vorticity. Above this depth, two vorticity thresholds delimit the unstable regime, outside of which the spectrum near the origin remains purely imaginary for all small Floquet exponents. In particular, at each fixed finite depth, constant vorticity of sufficiently large magnitude suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability. Moreover, any constant vorticity $γ\ge 2/\sqrt{3}$ suppresses Benjamin-Feir instability at every finite depth. The proof combines Hamiltonian spectral perturbation theory, symbolic computations, and formal verification in Rocq. Away from the transition set, our results rigorously confirm the stability criterion predicted by the nonlinear Schrödinger approximation of Thomas, Kharif, and Manna.
comments: This paper builds on our previous work arXiv:2610.39000 and reuses several technical results established there. Companion Mathematica notebooks and Rocq proof scripts are available upon request

title: Color Refinement Distinguishes Connected Rooted Outerplanar Graphs
abstract: Color refinement, also known as the $1$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm ($1$-WL), is a classical near-linear-time heuristic for graph isomorphism, which also captures the expressive power of message-passing graph neural networks. A long line of work asks on which graph classes $1$-WL, or its higher-dimensional variant $k$-WL, identifies every graph; the least such $k$ is the WL-dimension of the class. Planar graphs have WL-dimension at most $3$ (Kiefer, Ponomarenko and Schweitzer, 2019), and whether $2$-WL already distinguishes all planar graphs is a central open problem. We bring new insight on this question for outerplanar graphs, whose WL-dimension is $2$. We show that color refinement, i.e. 1-WL, distinguishes connected rooted outerplanar graphs: two non-isomorphic such graphs receive different stable colorings once a single vertex, the root, is individualized. The root is necessary, as there are non-isomorphic $2$-connected outerplanar graphs that color refinement does not distinguish. Our result extends to pseudo-rooted graphs, in which the stable coloring merely contains a singleton color class, and to non-connected graphs whose components all contain such a class. Consequently, the $(1,1)$-WL test of Rattan and Seppelt (2023) distinguishes all outerplanar graphs. We proceed by inversion: we reconstruct a connected rooted outerplanar graph, up to isomorphism, from its color graph, the weighted quotient of the graph by its stable color classes, together with its root color. The reconstruction runs in time linear in the output size and is canonical, which yields a near-linear-time canonization algorithm for these graphs. Our main tool is a dichotomy lemma, formalized in Rocq: in a rooted outerplanar graph with an equitable coloring, every block either receives pairwise distinct colors or admits a color-preserving mirror symmetry fixing its vertex closest to the root.

title: No free lattice contains an infinite ascending chain of copies of FL(3)
abstract: No free lattice contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of sublattices isomorphic to FL(3), the free lattice on three generators; this answers a question that R. A. Dean asked and the second author's 1997 notes on the problem left open. Every such chain would yield, inside FL(3), a coherent chain of proper self-embeddings $Θ_0, Θ_1, Θ_2, \dots$ with $Θ_k \circ Θ_j = Θ_j$ for $j < k$, so that each later embedding fixes the image of each earlier one pointwise. Every proper self-embedding of FL(3) whose fixed sublattice contains a free generating triple fixes one of the three generators, say $z$, because a power of it or of its dual lies above the identity, and a self-embedding that moves every generator and lies above the identity fixes at most eleven elements. Up to duality, a proper self-embedding fixing the image of such a $Θ_1$ pointwise fixes only elements above $z \wedge (x \vee y)$, where no free generating triple containing $z$ can lie. We also verify the one-step example of the 1997 notes, prove that no step toward such a chain is self-similar, and show that the configuration the argument rules out at length three does occur at length two. Without freeness the answer reverses: FL(3) contains an infinite strictly ascending chain of 3-generated sublattices, so the lattice analogue of Takahasi's chain condition for free groups fails. The theorem itself is checked by the Agda proof assistant under its safe flags, for free lattices over generators with decidable equality, and its formal proof uses no classical principle: finite searches and an induction on a finite set replace the infinite pigeonhole principle by which a chain yields a coherent chain.
comments: 59 pages, 13 figures; the main theorem is checked in Agda; the formal development is available at https://github.com/ualib/agda-deans-problem

title: Delaunay Combinatorics of the Moduli and Teichmüller Space of Closed Genus-Two Riemann Surfaces
abstract: Every closed Riemann surface of genus two is hyperelliptic, so it is determined by six branch points on the sphere, which become cone points of angle pi in the quotient orbifold metric. The Delaunay decomposition of these cone points, dual to the Voronoi diagram of the Weierstrass points, gives a trivalent graph with eight vertices, twelve edges and six faces. We classify these graphs. When the dual triangulation is simple there are exactly two types, dual to the octahedron and to a stacked triangulation, with orientation-preserving automorphism groups of orders 24 and 2, and we determine the Whitehead-move (diagonal-flip) orbit connecting them. Allowing bigons, the orbit closes at exactly twenty types. Iterated edge contraction from the two simple types gives a seven-level hierarchy of 2, 6, 22, 32, 22, 5 and 1 types, ending at two vertices joined by six parallel edges; closing under both contraction and expansion gives all 280 maps on the sphere with six vertices and no vertex of degree one. The rank of the linear cone-angle system of each type equals the real dimension 6 of the Teichmüller space. We realize both simple types by explicit hyperbolic cone spheres, in closed form for the octahedral type, build the corresponding genus-two surfaces by cutting and doubling, and show that the boundary x_e = 0 of the angle system is exactly the concyclicity of four branch points. The classification, the automorphism groups and the flip orbit are formally verified in Lean 4, and every enumeration is reproduced by an independent program, which also determines which types are realized by Delaunay decompositions.
comments: 29 pages, 10 figures. A Lean 4 formalization of the finite combinatorics and a verification script for all enumerations are available from the author

title: The cop number of the flower snarks, and the generalized Petersen graphs with cop number two
abstract: We study two questions of Morris, Runte and Skelton (Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022)) on the game of Cops and Robbers. First, we show that the flower snark $J_n$ has cop number $3$ for every $n\geq 5$, and that $J_3$ has cop number $2$. The upper bound comes from a three-cop strategy, which we call the rolling wall. It works on every connected graph whose vertices can be arranged in a cycle of columns, each dominated by a single vertex. Because only one cop moves on each turn, the same strategy also shows that the lazy cop number of $J_n$ is $3$ for $n\geq 5$. Second, we prove the conjecture of Morris, Runte and Skelton that the only generalized Petersen graphs with cop number $2$ are $\mathrm{GP}(n,1)$ and the four graphs $\mathrm{GP}(6,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(8,2)$, $\mathrm{GP}(9,3)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(12,3)$. The new ingredient is an explicit robber strategy showing that two cops do not suffice on $\mathrm{GP}(3k,k)$ and $\mathrm{GP}(4k,k)$ for $k\geq 4$. The theorem on flower snarks and all of the new lower bounds have been formally verified in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
comments: 9 pages, 1 figure, 1 table

title: Brunn-Minkowski inequalities for Riesz capacity in all dimensions
abstract: We prove the Brunn--Minkowski inequality for Riesz $p$-capacity on compact subsets of $\mathbb{R}^n$ when $n-1<p<n$, extending the known endpoint $p=n-1$. For sets of positive capacity, equality holds if and only if they are convex and positively homothetic. The inequality remains conjectural for $n-2<p<n-1$, when $n\ge2$. Known isodiametric counterexamples rule out a general extension to negative $p$, even for convex planar sets.
comments: 27 pages, 1 figure. A mathematical audit prepared by ChatGPT-6.1 Sol is included as an ancillary file

title: Fundamental Limits of Statistical Watermarking for LLMs with Fixed and Optimizable Common Randomness
abstract: Watermarking has emerged as an important technique for distinguishing AI-generated text from human-written text. However, most existing work is primarily empirical, relies on ad hoc watermarking designs, and lacks a fundamental understanding of the performance limits. In this paper, we propose a unified theoretical framework for statistical watermarking of large language models (LLMs), casting the problem as an independence test between generated text and common randomness and jointly designing the watermarking embedder and the detector. Our objective is to maximize detection power while controlling the worst-case false positive rate (FPR) and limiting distortion to text quality. A central focus of our framework is the design of the common randomness, which plays a critical role in both watermark embedding and detection. We characterize the fundamental limits of statistical watermarking under both fixed and optimizable common randomness. Our results show that optimizing the common randomness does not improve the fundamental limits: the best achievable performance is the same as that with fixed common randomness. Nevertheless, common randomness design remains highly important because it can substantially simplify detector design. In particular, with optimizable common randomness, a fixed, deterministic, and model-agnostic detector can achieve optimal performance. We further study a practical setting with fixed uniform common randomness and a fixed deterministic detector, and characterize its performance gap relative to the optimizable case, thereby demonstrating the practical value of optimizable common randomness.

title: The Bilinear Hilbert Transform Along the Primes
abstract: We prove that the discrete Bilinear Hilbert Transform along the primes, \begin{align} \mathcal{H}_{\mathbb{P}}(f,g)(x) := \sum_{n \neq 0} \frac{Λ(|n|)}{n} f(x-n) g(x+n), \qquad Λ(n) := \begin{cases} \log p & \text{ if } n = p^k, \ k \geq 1 \\ 0 & \text{ otherwise} \end{cases} \end{align} extends to a bounded operator from $\ell^p \times \ell^q \to \ell^r$ whenever $p,q \in (1,\infty)$ and $\frac{1}{r}=\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}$ in the Banach range, $r \geq 1$, and a particular portion of the quasi-Banach range $r \in \left(\frac{2}{3},1\right)$; in the diagonal case, this extends up to the endpoint $(\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{3},\frac{5}{6})$. After $U^3$-based reductions, the philosophy of the proof becomes similar to that of Krause-Mirek-Tao (on different bilinear operators in discrete harmonic analysis), namely a ``splitting" of the problem into an arithmetic component, handled by analysis within cyclic subgroups, and an analytic component, handled by analysis along arithmetic progressions. For the arithmetic component, we draw upon previous work of most of the authors on Carleson operators along the primes; the main analytic input are estimates for UMD space-valued bilinear singular integrals with modulation invariance, due to Di Plinio-Li-Martikainen-Vuorinen.
comments: Lean formalization at https://github.com/anastasiosfragkosmath/Prime_BHT_Palomar_Submission

title: From Objective Compromise to Structure-Enabled Intelligence: Reshaping the Scientific Paradigm of AI
abstract: Mainstream artificial intelligence systems, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), are fundamentally constructed upon the Optimization-Driven (OD) paradigm. This paradigm can be characterized as an ill-posed optimization problem within a high-dimensional parameter space. When confronted with real-world scenarios characterized by noise and conflicting constraints, the logic of global error minimization inherently induces a strong smoothing effect. Consequently, this yields statistical compromise solutions that flatten local features, making it arduous to overcome the inherent bottleneck of Out-of-Distribution (OOD) generalization. Existing AI models generate outputs purely based on statistical probabilities. They lack the capacity to autonomously discern truth from falsehood or establish causal logic, thereby lacking genuine cognitive intelligence. To address the ontological limitations of the OD paradigm, this paper proposes a novel paradigm termed \textit{Structure-Enabled Intelligence}. This approach abandons the conventional path of relying solely on computing power scaling and data fitting to achieve emergent intelligence. Instead, it embeds mathematical structures and physical mechanisms as underlying priors into the algorithmic architecture, constraining the model's solving process with structured scientific rules. Through this paradigm shift from ``data-driven objective fitting'' to ``mechanism-structure dominance,'' the proposed approach fundamentally mitigates the issue of statistical compromise, enhances the model's extrapolation and generalization capabilities, and simultaneously reshapes human-AI synergy by upholding human subjectivity in scientific cognition.

title: On $z_{2M}(21,4)$: the Hole Extensions of the Chen--Chen Configuration Are Reducible, and the Extremal Configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ Are Not Unique
abstract: The second order extended Zarankiewicz number $z_{2M}(m,n)$ of Qi and Yu allows a secondary half of a $2$-edge to be shared, while the $1$-edge graph stays $C_4$-free and extremal and $1$-edges and main halves stay exclusive. Whether $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ is open. Since deleting a $2$-edge removes exactly one displayed square, $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ if and only if there is no irreducible admissible configuration with exactly $56$ displayed squares, and by the cell count of Qi and Yu and the heredity of irreducibility such a configuration without empty cells is an extremal $55$-square configuration of $z_2(21,4)$ plus one $2$-edge at its hole. For the extremal configuration of Chen and Chen we show, by certificates verified in exact rational arithmetic, that all $56$ such extensions have SOS rank at most $55$: $32$ by product relations and $24$ by contraction certificates of Xu--Yan type. We also show, with computer-assisted certificates and an exhaustive isomorphism search, that the extremal configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ fall into at least six isomorphism classes; Chen and Chen leave the structural classification of extremal augmented graphs open. Finally we prove a six-to-four reduction. For irreducible configurations whose $1$-edge graph is $C_4$-free with $m+\binom n2$ edges it bounds the multiplicity of a shared half by $n(n-1)$ ($12$ at $21\times4$), and it applies directly to an explicit number of the extensions of any extremal configuration of $z_2(21,4)$, eight for that of Chen and Chen, bringing each to at most $54$ squares, in agreement with the certificates. The cell count, the heredity lemma, the rows lemma, the six-to-four identity and a $2\times2$ example are checked in Isabelle/HOL; the remaining arguments are written proofs.

title: Generic finiteness of rotating relative equilibria in the planar $N$-vortex problem
abstract: For every $N\ge2$, we prove that Zariski-generic nonzero real circulations, with any prescribed signs, admit at most $N^{2N}$ labeled, collision-free rotating relative equilibria modulo translations, rotations in $SO(2)$, and positive scaling. The excluded parameters lie in an explicit finite union of quadratic hypersurfaces. The proof combines a logarithmic-residue obstruction to positive-dimensional complex solution sets with Bézout degree bounds.
comments: 8 pages. Comments welcome. The work was done with the help of AI

title: Maximality of the Došen--Petrić Boolean Category
abstract: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Došen and Petrić, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining any equation between parallel morphisms that does not follow from the defining equations, and closing under the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal. The proof uses Boolean Coherence to select a pair of variable occurrences on which the two morphisms differ. Composition with morphisms selecting these occurrences, uniform substitution and two isomorphisms yield equality of the product projections. We prove that any zero-identity Boolean category satisfying such an additional equation under every interpretation of the variables is a preorder. We also give a Lean formalization of these proofs and their dependencies. It includes Boolean Coherence and the correspondence between substitution on tagged occurrence sets and substitution on finite ordinals.
comments: 23 pages. Lean formalization: https://palomar-registry.org/entry?id=PALOMAR-2026-10-30-000014&version=3

title: A New Record for the Katz-Tao Sum-Difference Exponent
abstract: We prove the record bound $C_{3b}\le 209357544569848128/114631769327023765=1.8263483657186\ldots$ for the Katz-Tao sum-difference exponent, valid in every abelian group without $2$-torsion. Using only Shannon inequalities, conditional copies and Katz-Tao's original directions, whose classical single-grid argument gives $11/6$, we break $11/6$, obtaining $2762/1509$ and $152/83$. For every abelian group we prove the universal bound $C_{\mathrm{all}}=10304335425987192362/5641833174538280329=1.8264161855212\ldots$, which is below the previous record for the real Katz-Tao constant. In the AlphaEvolve study (arXiv:2511.02864v3), the search for extremal distributions improved this constant's lower bound in the eighth decimal place and left its upper bound at $11/6$. Our upper bounds are proofs discovered by CASPAC, the computational mathematics engine of the CASP research system, and certified by independent exact checkers. The proofs use stacked entropy certificates; we supply the complete rational identities, proofs of every auxiliary inequality, and exact verification over the stated group classes.
comments: 14 pages, 2 figures. Complete proof certificates and exact verification code included as ancillary files

title: On the number of elite primes
abstract: A prime $p$ is elite if all sufficiently large Fermat numbers $F_n=2^{2^n}+1$ are quadratic nonresidues modulo $p$. Let $E(x)$ be the number of elite primes up to $x$. The best published bounds are $E(x)\ll x/(\log x)^{3/2}$ unconditionally and $E(x)\ll x^{5/6}$ under the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis (GRH), both due to Just. Just and Pollack remarked, without a written proof, that sorting primes by the exact power of $2$ dividing $p-1$ should give $x/(\log x)^{2-\varepsilon}$ and $x^{3/4+\varepsilon}$. We give complete proofs of slightly sharper statements: $E(x)\le(16+o(1))x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$ unconditionally, and $E(x)\ll x^{3/4}(\log x)^{1/2}$ under GRH. We also recall, with short proofs, known facts about the period of $(F_n\bmod p)$ that go back to Aigner: every elite prime $p$ satisfies the defining condition from the index $v_2(\operatorname{ord}_p 2)$ onwards, and the period is even unless $p\in\{3,5\}$. Finally, we show under GRH that, when the moduli involved are at most $x^{1/3}$, the set of primes bounded by the sieve argument has size $\asymp x\log\log x/(\log x)^2$. This indicates that the remaining factor $\log\log x$ cannot be removed by this method alone. All theorems of the paper have been formalized in the Lean 4 proof assistant, with the Brun--Titchmarsh inequality and two standard consequences of GRH as explicit hypotheses.
comments: 11 pages. Includes a Lean 4 formalization with three analytic inputs as explicit hypotheses

title: A Hierarchical Statistical Framework for Evaluating Agent Reliability
abstract: Agents operating in complex scenarios often face uncertainty due to incomplete information about the environment they operate in, ambiguous user queries, complex business rules and the inherently stochastic dynamics of the governing policy. Several new benchmarks have been proposed to evaluate LLM-based agents on complex tasks in multi-tool environments, including settings with policy constraints and varying levels of intent ambiguity. These conditions make it important to evaluate agentic systems systematically and quantify their performance under different conditions to assess their reliability in production. This need is evident in the recently introduced Thinkingbox benchmark, where even the strongest models struggle to perform consistently across diverse business scenarios. This paper presents a statistical framework for evaluating uncertainty and reliability in agentic systems. We define a hierarchy of scenarios, instances, and samples to assess model performance and variability systematically. We apply this framework to common metrics found in the literature: mean pass rate, $pass@k$, and $passhat^k$, with uncertainty estimates for each metric. Aggregating metrics at different levels of the hierarchy reveals different structures and properties of the policy model; we connect this hierarchical aggregation with the known process of \emph{coarse-graining} as intended in the physics and statistical literature. We independently derive exact finite-sample expressions for the sampling variances of the unbiased $pass@k$ and $passhatk$ estimators; related results also appear in recent submissions. Our central contribution is a constructive derivation of hierarchical uncertainty propagation, making explicit its correspondence with coarse-graining and separating execution noise from task heterogeneity.

title: Spectral Moments of the Projected Hubbard Configuration Graph: Connectivity, Exchange, and Virtual Doublons
abstract: At strong on-site repulsion, the lowest band of $n$ lattice fermions is the spectrum of the hopping projected onto configurations without double occupancy, $H_\infty=P_0H_tP_0$. We study its moments, for few fermions in the square-lattice Hubbard model and, where the arguments allow, on any finite graph. (1) For spin-independent Hermitian hopping (no on-site terms) on any $N\geq2$-site graph, $μ_2=\frac{n(N-n)}{N(N-1)}\sum_{i\neq j}|t_{ij}|^2$, for any spin composition. (2) On any finite graph, $μ_4$ is exactly linear in the same-spin pair count, as four hops permute particles by at most a transposition or 3-cycle; for uniform hopping on a simple graph with $N\geq4$ the slope is $α(N,n)=-8C_4(N-n)(8N-11n-2)/[N(N-1)(N-2)(N-3)]$, fixed by the number $C_4$ of 4-cycles. (3) At large finite $U$, the second-order Schrieffer-Wolff correction is Hilbert-Schmidt orthogonal to $H_\infty$ on every triangle-free graph, so the band variance has no $1/U$ term; its $U^{-2}$ coefficient, an exact trace checked by exact diagonalization, is negative at the low fillings computed. (4) Under a Peierls flux, the exchange slope $α(N,2,Φ)=-\frac{64}{N-1}\cosΦ_\square$ ($L\times L$ tori, $L=3$ or $L\geq5$) carries the ordinary charge-$e$ harmonic, while the doublon (bound-pair) hopping acquires a doubled phase, $t_de^{2iA_{ij}}$: the second-order single-doublon Hamiltonian is exactly $π$-periodic ($h/2e$) under a boundary twist, and the exact two-electron U-band follows numerically, up to $O((2λ)^L/U^{L-1})$. Result (1), the permutation bound, the orthogonality in (3) and the doubled phase are machine-checked in Lean 4. Repulsive binding and the pair charge $2e$ are known; new are the exact moment structure and the derivation of the doubled phase. We make no claim about many-pair phase stiffness, off-diagonal long-range order or superconductivity.
comments: 42 pages, 11 figures, 7 tables; Supplemental Material (notes S1-S12, 142 pages) as ancillary file. Code, Lean 4 formalization and run records: https://github.com/zhineos/hubbard-spectral-moments, doi:10.5281/zenodo.24244237

title: Strong Standard Completeness of a Hypersequent Calculus for Cyclic Involutive Residuated Lattices
abstract: We present a hypersequent calculus $H_R$ for cyclic involutive residuated lattices and prove strong standard completeness for arbitrary theories in a fixed countable propositional language. Standard models are chains on $[0,1]$; neither commutativity nor equality of the monoid unit and the dualizing constant is assumed. The chain semantics is the class $K_R$ defined by unit cyclicity and all ordered finite-history conditions. Every countable member of $K_R$ embeds into a standard chain preserving the entire signature. The construction combines central-support reconstruction, gap insertion and relative contraction. A relative comparison construction supplies the required chain countermodels. We also prove admissibility of the unrestricted density rule for theoremhood and effective elimination from finite proofs without additional assumption leaves. Elimination uses terminating enumeration of density-free proofs; ordinary Cut is retained, and no complexity bound is claimed. Further constructions give bounded standard embeddings for nontrivial countable chains of involutive uninorm logic and pseudo-uninorm logic with weak commutativity. Using ordinary chain completeness for arbitrary theories, these yield strong standard completeness for both logics. A companion Lean~4 development formalizes the main results, with its scope and external inputs stated explicitly.
comments: 102 pages

title: A formally verified convergence theorem for the tug-of-war scheme of the normalized $p$-Laplacian
abstract: We present a complete formalization, using Lean 4, of the convergence of $p$-harmonious functions to the viscosity solution of the Dirichlet problem for the normalized $p$-Laplacian, $2 \le p < \infty$, as the step size goes to zero. By $p$-harmonious functions we mean solutions of the dynamic programming principle of tug-of-war with noise. Our proof follows the argument of Barles and Souganidis and is formalized in full, depending only on Mathlib and the standard axioms of Lean. In particular, we include the asymptotic expansion of the scheme, the viscosity properties of the half-relaxed limits, existence and uniqueness for the discrete problem, the comparison principle and uniqueness for the homogeneous equation, Aleksandrov's theorem, and Jensen's lemma.
comments: 14 pages, 1 figure. Lean 4 source: https://github.com/BehroozMoosavi/tugofwar_formalization (tag v1.3). Blueprint and browsable formal statements: https://behroozmoosavi.github.io/tugofwar_formalization/

title: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three
abstract: We study the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups through signed identities among zero-sum subsequences. An integral incidence identity of degree $t$ for a sequence assigns integer weights to its nonempty zero-sum subsequences so that the weights add up to one, while those of the subsequences containing any given nonempty set of at most $t$ terms add up to zero. Over a finite abelian $p$-group $H$, the zero-sum subsequences of a sequence of any length have an indicator polynomial of degree at most $D(H)-1$, and this gives a transfer principle: if, for each $t\ge0$, every sequence of $L(t)$ terms over $Q$ admits such an identity of degree $t$, then $D(Q\oplus H)\le L(D(H)-1)$ for every finite abelian $p$-group $H$. For $m\in\{2,3,4\}$ we construct integral identities at length $L(t)=m(t+3)-2$ over $C_m^3$, and prove that these thresholds are sharp over fields of characteristic zero or characteristic not dividing $m$. For a prime $p\nmid m$ and $0\le a\le b\le c$, we prove that \[ D(C_{mp^a}\oplus C_{mp^b}\oplus C_{mp^c}) =m(p^a+p^b+p^c)-2. \] In particular $D(C_{15}^3)=43$ and $D(C_{20}^3)=58$, which are the two smallest cases of the conjecture $D(C_n^3)=3n-2$ left open in the literature. The proofs of the base cases for $m \in \{3,4\}$ are computer-assisted. All of the results in this paper have been formalised in Lean 4.
comments: the mathematical arguments are on the first 13 pages; comments are welcomed

title: Ramsey sets are canonically Ramsey
abstract: A set $A$ of points is called Ramsey if, for each $r$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $A$. We show that for each Ramsey set $A$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space, regardless of the number of colors used, contains a monochromatic or a rainbow congruent copy of $A$. This answers a question raised in virtually every paper on the topic.
comments: 8+2 pages, early announcement mainly due to ChatGPT-6 Astra, will be replaced shortly

title: Sharp bounds on the Eliashberg critical temperature: a comparison principle, convexity in the spectrum, and the Kiessling-Altshuler-Yuzbashyan conjectures
abstract: In Eliashberg theory of phonon-mediated superconductivity with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential, the critical temperature $T_c$ marks the linear instability of the normal state. Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan (KAY) characterized it through the top eigenvalue of a compact operator on Matsubara-frequency sequences. They proved that $T_c$ is unique at strong coupling and conjectured $T_c<C(λ\langleω^2\rangle)^{1/2}$ for every coupling $λ$, with $\langleω^2\rangle$ the second moment of the normalized phonon spectrum and $C\approx0.1827$ sharp, a bound Leavens stated in 1977 on partly numerical grounds. A preprint by Kondratev, not yet peer reviewed, gives a proof of this bound and of all-coupling uniqueness. We give an independent proof, for every spectrum with finite second moment, based on a comparison principle that is also Kondratev's central step and was proved to first order by Bergmann and Rainer: strengthening the pairing interaction at every Matsubara transfer, strictly at the smallest one, strictly raises the top eigenvalue. At fixed $λ$ and $\langleω^2\rangle$ a single Einstein mode maximizes $T_c$. Convexity of the top eigenvalue in the spectrum gives sharp bounds on $T_c$ by the moments $\intω^nα^2F dω$, $0\le n\le1$, including Leavens's zeroth-moment bound $T_c\le c_0\intα^2F dω$, $c_0\approx0.231$ numerically, optimal at moderate coupling. All bounds persist under a Coulomb pseudopotential with symmetric cutoff. A prefix decomposition of non-increasing vectors proves a third KAY conjecture, not treated in the preprint. The finite-dimensional core, including that conjecture, is formalized in Lean 4, and two computer-assisted proofs independent of the comparison principle confirm the Einstein bound.
comments: 23 pages, 2 figures. Lean 4 formalization of the finite-dimensional core, two computer-assisted certificates and all scripts are in the ancillary files

title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for unique equilibrium states
abstract: Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension at least three, $φ:M\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and $R\ge2$ be an integer. We construct a $\mathcal C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ and an observable $f\in\mathcal C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ such that $(T,φ)$ has a unique equilibrium state $μ$ and $μ(f)=0$. The system $(T,μ)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ but not of order $R+1$ for Hölder observables, and $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f\circ T^i$ does not satisfy the central limit theorem. The main results have been formalised in Lean 4.
comments: 39 pages, 0 figures

title: Gorenstein toric Fano $d$-varieties have Picard ranks at most $2d$
abstract: We show that the Picard rank of $d$-dimensional Gorenstein toric Fano varieties is at most $2d$. This generalizes Batyrev's conjecture of Picard ranks for smooth toric Fano varieties, which was proved by Casagrande for all $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial Gorenstein toric Fano varieties. The convex-geometric proof is a generalization of Casagrande's proof and Eikelberg's theory of non-$\mathbb{Q}$-factorial toric Picard groups, with key ideas from work of Debarre, Øbro, Fujita and the first author. The proof was found using ChatGPT 6.1.
comments: 1 figure. 10 pages. Comments are welcome!

title: Ice and mirrors
abstract: Given a mirror pair of smooth affine principal upper cluster varieties admitting reddening sequences, we show that homological mirror symmetry for principal cluster varieties -- assumed compatible with certain cluster structures -- descends under freezing. This allows us to induct on the following class. A skew-symmetrizable matrix is peelable if, by mutations and removing sinks or sources, it can be reduced to the empty matrix; it is sub-peelable if it is a principal submatrix of a peelable matrix. We establish homological mirror symmetry for full rank upper cluster varieties whose mutable matrix is sub-peelable. We show sub-peelability for the Fock--Goncharov SL(n) quiver for any compact surface with nonempty boundary, all of whose boundaries have markings. Consequently, we establish homological mirror symmetry between the moduli of decorated SL(n) local systems and the corresponding pinned PGL(n) spaces. The results were obtained using ChatGPT Astra.
comments: 57 pages

title: Trustworthy Numerical Software in the Age of AI: What Would Turing Do?
abstract: AI coding agents can now produce numerical software faster than human experts can review it, raising serious concerns about usability and reliability. These and other AI tools are already transforming mathematics and software, and they will soon transform mathematical software. These concerns motivated us to assess AI-generated numerical linear algebra (NLA) kernels, which we did through an audit of a recent public GPU QR competition. All five leading kernels passed the competition's accuracy tests, and the winning kernel achieved a 107-fold speedup over the competition's baseline, which calls NVIDIA's QR routine. Yet each failed at least once on new inputs, even those from the competition's generator, under the same checker, while the baseline passed them all. In light of this, we want to develop reusable formalizations of numerical analysis methods, which remain sparsely represented in existing formal libraries. We describe VSCL, our Lean library of mathematical foundations for numerical computing. We also propose VERNA to connect these tasks by using formalized results to guide kernel assessment against explicit specifications. Drawing on Turing's work on rounding-error analysis and program checking, we discuss design principles for developing trustworthy numerical software when direct human checking is impractical.
comments: 44 pages

title: Hidden convexity of the Eliashberg condensation energy: existence, uniqueness and continuity of the superconducting state
abstract: Kiessling, Altshuler and Yuzbashyan conjectured the thermodynamic transition picture for the isotropic Eliashberg spin-chain functional with vanishing Coulomb pseudopotential: the normal state is the unique minimizer above and at a critical temperature, the superconducting minimizer below it is unique up to gauge, and the transition is continuous. We establish the nonlinear part of this picture. In the variables $ρ_n=\sin^2θ_n$, the condensation energy restricted to the first quadrant is strictly convex, and folding any admissible chain into that quadrant cannot increase its energy. For every positive, non-increasing interaction with power-law decay, hidden convexity and a compactness estimate give existence and uniqueness of the minimizer up to gauge. The normal state minimizes the energy exactly when its quadratic form is non-negative, including marginal stability. Among admissible chains, a positive solution of the nonlinear Eliashberg equations exists exactly when the normal state is linearly unstable and is then unique. For temperature-dependent families with pointwise continuity and locally uniform decay bounds, the minimizing density is continuous in a weighted $\ell^1$ norm. Together with uniqueness of the linear-stability temperature, these results prove the thermodynamic conjectures for the $γ$-model, Einstein phonons and general phonon spectra; the phonon applications use separately established spectral input. Finite-dimensional algebraic and convex-analytic components are machine-checked in Lean. The proofs were obtained independently of concurrent work that reaches overlapping conclusions.
comments: 23 pages, 2 figures. Companion to "Sharp bounds on the Eliashberg critical temperature: a comparison principle, convexity in the spectrum, and the Kiessling-Altshuler-Yuzbashyan conjectures" (D. Rens, submitted). Lean 4 formalization of the finite-dimensional core and the numerical study are in the ancillary files

title: Simultaneous analysis of approximate leave-one-out cross-validation and mean-field inference II: General convex penalties
abstract: For smooth penalties and group Lasso, analyzed approximate leave-one-out (ALO) cross-validation by comparing its weights with the trace correction used in mean-field inference. For a $C^2$ penalty $R$, the matrix entering these corrections is $A=[\nabla^2R(\widehat b)+X^TDX]^{-1}$, where $\widehat b$ is the full-data estimator and $D$ is the diagonal matrix of fitted loss curvatures; for group Lasso, the penalty and loss curvatures are first restricted to the active support before taking the pseudoinverse. The obstacle to extending this argument to general convex penalties was the lack of an explicit formula for the matrix $A$ entering these corrections. For every finite-valued strongly convex penalty, we construct such a matrix from ordinary derivatives of the penalty response at the observed subgradient. Its projection--pseudoinverse formula separates the response space and penalty curvature, fixed by conditioning, from the explicit design dependence. This supplies the missing ingredient to extend the probabilistic argument of Part~I. The construction recovers the inverse Hessian for smooth penalties and the active-group inverse for group Lasso, including inactive boundary groups. In the proportional regime, for Gaussian designs with general positive-definite covariance and covariance-scaled strong convexity, we obtain unconditional bounds comparing both ALO and mean-field predictions with exact leave-one-out predictions in regression and single-index models. The expected average squared prediction error is $O(n^{-1})$, and the expected absolute criterion error is $O(n^{-1/2})$, under bounded, 1-Lipschitz loss scores and suitable test functions. The matrix and ALO weights use only observed data; the mean-field correction additionally uses the design covariance. The construction, recovery identities and statistical guarantees are formalized in Lean~4.
comments: Part I is available at https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.02624. Lean files can be found in the arXiv ancillary files

title: The BMM symmetrising trace conjecture for all exceptional complex reflection groups
abstract: We prove the symmetrising trace conjecture of Broué, Malle and Michel for the generic Hecke algebras of all exceptional complex reflection groups. A key ingredient is a new family of bases, constructed via breadth-first search, which generalise the standard basis of an Iwahori-Hecke algebra. These bases provide a uniform proof of the freeness conjecture of Broué, Malle and Rouquier for these groups. The verification for each group reduces to a finite computation, carried out using programs developed with the assistance of a large language model.

title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
abstract: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names. We build a bridge between them. To describe, we condense about 200 papers into the Three-Clock Dictionary, which maps fifteen concepts of nonlinear dynamics onto each clock and marks every correspondence as proved, measured or conjectured, and we show each concept in a mechanical system and in a language model side by side. To explain, we derive reduced-order models: the softmax is a Boltzmann distribution, gradient descent an Euler step on a nonlinear spring, a loss spike a ball thrown out of a stiff valley, attention on the circle a Kuramoto model, and a repetition loop a well that deepens while it is occupied. We then test these explanations on open language models, on a laptop CPU. Escape from repetition loops in GPT-2 and Pythia follows the Arrhenius law with the logit gap as the barrier, and the barrier deepens and then saturates, so the temperature needed to leave a loop falls like $1/\ln N$ with the generation length $N$ and rises with model size. Coherent text lives in a narrow window of temperatures, which a small reasoning model shares at its recommended temperature. Training makes each Pythia layer more expansive, and a small transformer trains at a multi-mode edge of stability. The third step, solving problems of language models, is still ahead: controllers derived from the escape analysis remove loops but do not yet beat the best fixed temperature. We state twelve open problems where nonlinear dynamics could get there.
comments: 52 pages, 19 figures. Code and data: https://github.com/maorfarid1/three-clocks

title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
abstract: We propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding (CPTC), a low-bit quantization format for tensors written once and read many times. Formats that round each value on its own, such as INT4 and FP4, waste a large part of their bits against the information-theoretic ideal. Trellis codes recover this loss by encoding values jointly, but prior decoders either need a large lookup table for their best quality or compute values with a hash that restricts what they can decode. CPTC's decoder multiplies its state by two coefficients and adds the top bits of the products to index a 64-byte table. Because that sum is not uniformly distributed, the rarely used ends of a small table can hold values far out in the tails. One decoder serves every bit width from 1 to 6, reproduces the standard integer and floating-point formats exactly, and comes within 0.07 bits of the ideal at 4 bits. It matches a random-permutation trellis code whose table is thousands of times larger, and exceeds every QTIP codebook. In LLM weight quantization without fine-tuning, CPTC has the lowest KL divergence to the unquantized model at every tested bit width on Llama 3.1 8B and 70B Instruct against QTIP's codebooks (by up to 27%). The decoder has been built into the AWS Trainium 4 AI accelerator, where it runs at the throughput of the native FP4 and FP8 formats for a negligible fraction of the systolic array's area. Fused encoding kernels quantize an 8B model's linear layers in under two minutes on one GPU and, in cycle-level simulation, on one Trainium 4 chip.
comments: 38 pages, 6 figures, 27 tables

title: FunSearch and Structured SAT Search for Weak Schur Partitions
abstract: The weak Schur problem asks how large an interval of consecutive integers can be partitioned into a fixed number of classes with no class containing a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$ with $a\neq b$. We investigate whether FunSearch, an evolutionary program-search method guided by a large language model, can discover effective construction strategies for this classical combinatorial problem. In our adaptation, FunSearch evolves a priority function used by a fixed greedy solver, while a separate validity check enforces the weakly sum-free condition. This approach matches the known exact values for two, three, and four classes and reaches $WS(5)\geq195$. We then explore a complementary SAT-based approach. Guided by structural information from a 207-element construction communicated by Fred Rowley (Rowley, 2026), our SAT search produces and verifies a distinct valid five-class partition of $\{1,\ldots,207\}$. Thus the strongest construction obtained in this project reaches $WS(5)\geq207$, eleven integers beyond the best published lower bound of 196. The contrast between the two approaches also exposes a limitation of our FunSearch formulation: its greedy solver makes local, irreversible decisions, whereas SAT can enforce global structure across the whole partition.
comments: 9 pages, 1 figure, 4 tables

title: A Little Advice Suffices: Diffie-Hellman Is as Hard as Discrete Logarithm
abstract: Is computing a Diffie-Hellman key as hard as computing a discrete logarithm? Maurer showed that it is, given a few bits of advice, provided that short intervals contain enough integers with only small prime factors; that proviso has stood for thirty years. We remove it. For every prime $p$ there is an advice string of $O(\log p)$ bits, depending only on $p$, with which discrete logarithms in every group of order $p$ are computed in polynomial time from a Diffie-Hellman oracle. The reduction is the classical one; what was missing was a proof that short intervals contain polylogarithmically smooth integers. We show that a zero-free half-plane for the Riemann zeta function, which is now known, gives the expected number of $(\log x)^K$-smooth integers in every interval $[x,x+x^θ]$ with $θ>17/30$. With smoothness this small the saddle point of the counting integral lies just to the left of the line $\mathrm{Re}\,s=1$, and a zero-free strip of any fixed width absorbs the shift once $K$ is large. Genus-2 Jacobians, whose orders fill such intervals, then turn one of these integers into the order of an auxiliary group. The same input removes the smoothness assumption from Maurer and Raub's impossibility of field-homomorphic one-way permutations and from the yes/no-query reduction of Koblitz, Menezes and Shparlinski. It also makes Wolf's characterisation unconditional: discrete logarithm and Diffie-Hellman are generically equivalent exactly when the group order has no large repeated prime factor.
comments: 15 pages. Developed with Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic); see "Use of AI". Companion paper on the hyperelliptic curve method: https://github.com/OctopusTide/hyperelliptic-curve-method

title: Equivalence of Small and Large Quasi-kernels
abstract: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set which can reach every vertex of $D$ by a directed path of length at most 2. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture states that every $n$-vertex source-free digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|Q|\le n/2$, and the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture states that every $n$-vertex digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|N^+[Q]|\ge n/2$. Our main result shows for any $\frac{1}{2}<β<1$ an equivalence between the following two statements: \[\textrm{Every }n\textrm{-vertex source-free digraph contains a quasi-kernel with } |Q|\le n-Ω(n^β).\] \[\textrm{Every }n\textrm{-vertex digraph contains a quasi-kernel with } |N^+[Q]|\ge Ω(n^{2-\frac{1}β}).\] That is, any sublinear bound for one problem is equivalent to a corresponding sublinear bound for the other. This combined with previous work establishing an equivalence for linear bounds shows that the two problems are largely equivalent to each other. We additionally give a slight refinement to the recent breakthrough of Rutschmann for these problems which, together with the result above, gives the best known bounds of $n-Ω(n^{3/4})$ and $Ω(n^{2/3})$ for the Small and Large Quasi-kernel Conjectures, respectively. Our proofs are due to ChatGPT's Astra 6; the writing is all our own.
comments: 11 pages. The proofs are due to Astra 6, the writing is our own. Comments welcome!

title: Stratonovich Waves Driven by Space-Time Gaussian Noise
abstract: Motivated by Xia Chen's moment conjecture, we determine the exact second-moment asymptotics of the Stratonovich hyperbolic Anderson model in dimensions $d\in\{1,2,3\}$, driven by a centered Gaussian noise with temporal covariance $|s-t|^{-α_0}$ and an even, nonnegative, positive-definite tempered Radon spatial covariance $Γ$ homogeneous of order $-α$, where $0<α_0<1$, $0<α<d$ or $α=d=1$, and $α+α_0<2$. For initial displacement one and velocity zero, our main result is that $T^{-κ}\log\mathbb{E}u^2(T,x)$ converges, for every fixed $x$, to a constant $C_2(Γ,α_0)$, where $κ=(4-α-α_0)/(3-α)$. The constant is given by an intrinsic variational formula: a supremum over nonnegative smooth compactly supported space-time controls of twice the time integral of the square root of a Rayleigh value built from the covariance mean, minus half of the covariance variance. The variational class includes controls that do not separate in time and space, and the formula retains the original covariance amplitude, kinetic coefficient one and Gaussian cost. The constant is positive and finite when $Γ\neq0$. An independent upper bound establishes finiteness at the scale $T^κ$. The identification of the constant combines Gaussian phase operators, convergence from the regularized noise, estimates uniform in the spatial localization radius, and finite optimization with nonnegative Gram entries. We also bound the constant through spatial energies and occupation measures, with explicit bounds for spatial white noise in one dimension. The work was developed with AI assistance; the proofs have not yet been checked line by line by a human reader, and a public verification ledger records the status of each result.
comments: Version 1.0.0; 476 pages. Source, development history and verification ledger: https://github.com/chenle02/stratonovich-ham-second-moment (release v1.0.0). Lean companion: https://github.com/chenle02/stratonovich-ham-second-moment-lean (release v0.10.0, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24295453). Developed with AI assistance; see AI-USE-STATEMENT.md in the repository

title: $p$-harmonic polynomials
abstract: We prove that every real polynomial $p$-harmonic function on $\Rn$ is affine when $n\ge3$ and $p\ge n-1/13$. The proof uses the Bernstein--Szegő inequality on great circles and a deficit estimate at the first Chebyshev node.
comments: The Lean code and an explanation of the formalization process are available at https://github.com/na0b/pharmonicpoly-lean

title: Goemans's Unsplittable-Flow Conjecture: The Anatomy of AI-Assisted Counterexample Discovery
abstract: Goemans conjectured that any fractional single-source flow could be converted into an unsplittable flow without increasing total cost and while increasing any arc load by at most the largest demand. Recently, Dmitry Rybin announced a seven-vertex counterexample found through an interaction with ChatGPT, which disproved this long-standing conjecture. However, the interaction did not reveal why this particular topology and its demand, fractional-flow, and cost choices work together, whether the example belongs to a broader family, or which structural features determine where counterexamples can occur. It also left unclear why the AI-assisted search succeeded where earlier human efforts had not. In this paper, we develop a forward counterexample construction pipeline. It starts from an arborescence on which failure is impossible and adds terminal-entering shortcut arcs. The resulting load constraints define a finite set of admissible route choices; their convex hull, the conflict polytope, yields exact conditions for demands, fractional flows, and costs. Starting from a simple arborescence, the pipeline selects Rybin's topology and characterizes all counterexamples it supports. Experiments further demonstrate the pipeline's transferability: when instructed to follow it while varying the initial arborescence and shortcut placement, ChatGPT produced counterexamples on topologies genuinely different from Rybin's and found valid constructions starting from 93 other rooted arborescence shapes. The theory also explains why the original example was difficult to discover through blind enumeration and suggests that Rybin's interaction lies between blind enumeration and a complete theory-guided construction.

title: Existence of SRB measures for some Rössler systems
abstract: We prove that for the Rössler system $\dot x=-(y+z)$, $\dot y=x+ay$, $\dot z=b+z(x-c)$ with $a=b=0.2$, the set of parameters $c$ within $6\cdot10^{-5}$ of the classical value $c=5.7$ for which the flow has a Hénon-like strange attractor supporting a Sinai--Ruelle--Bowen (SRB) measure has positive Lebesgue measure. The key step, proved with computer assistance, is that at a parameter localised in an explicit interval within $5.5\cdot10^{-5}$ of $5.7$ the period-one saddle of the Poincaré map has a quadratic homoclinic tangency that unfolds generically; the conclusion then follows from the theorems of Mora--Viana, Benedicks--Young and Benedicks--Viana. The same method gives two further such tangencies near $5.7$ and one at the band-merging parameter $c\approx4.507$. The proof reduces the generic-tangency conditions to finitely many inequalities, through explicit $C^2$ graph-transform bounds for the local invariant manifolds of a Poincaré map whose area contraction is of order $10^{-11}$--$10^{-14}$, and a scalar tangency function. The inequalities are checked with interval arithmetic in CAPD and re-checked with an independent implementation based on the Kv library; the analytic tangency criterion is formalised in Lean~4. Whether an SRB measure exists at $c=5.7$ itself remains open.

title: Error Analysis of Deep Learning
abstract: This review examines deep learning theory through the lens of error decomposition, systematically addressing approximation, statistical, and optimization errors. We trace the development of error analyses from bounds on individual error components to frameworks that account for all three. Using nonparametric regression and the Deep Ritz Method as dual running examples, we demonstrate how these analyses apply across fundamentally different loss structures. We then review representative analyses in scientific machine learning, generative learning, reinforcement learning, representation learning, and large language models, showing how learning errors affect solutions, distributions, and predictions through problem-specific arguments. Throughout, we clarify which error components are controlled, how they are combined, and what assumptions are needed to obtain guarantees for trained networks.
comments: Mathematical survey of error analysis for neural network methods, with nonparametric regression and the Deep Ritz method for elliptic PDEs as running examples. Covers function and Sobolev approximation, statistical estimation, and optimization error, together with stability estimates, convergence rates, and selected proofs

title: Higher-order estimates for $p$-harmonic functions in the plane
abstract: Closing a longstanding gap in the theory, we establish uniform interior $C^{k,β}$ estimates for planar $p$-harmonic functions with $1<p<2$. These estimates hold for every integer $k\ge2$ and every $0<β<1$ such that $k+β<s(p)$, where $s(p)$ is the optimal regularity order identified by Iwaniec and Manfredi. As consequences, we obtain decay estimates at critical points, a Liouville theorem with optimal growth exponent, and uniform higher-order estimates for the flux of planar $q$-harmonic functions with $q>2$.
comments: The Lean code and a description of the formalization process are available at https://github.com/na0b/phigherorder-lean

title: Formally Verified Semidefinite Programming
abstract: We present a formally verified Rust implementation of a first-order semidefinite programming solver, a nontrivial piece of numerical software. We wrote the solver by hand and then directed Claude to generate the entire verification in Verus, an automated theorem prover for Rust programs. We discuss the algorithm underlying the solver, its implementation in Rust, and our pragmatic approach to proving it correct in Verus.
comments: 9 pages. Comments welcome

title: Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture
abstract: Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture. Reducing the characteristic polynomial modulo $4$ gives a necessary condition for nilpotency that is linear over $\F$. For $m > 1$ it forces $u = (v, 1, i, \rev v)$ or $u = (v, i, 1, \rev v)$, and an identity implicit in Corless's proof then reduces the problem to $v$. Since $T_m(u)$ is diagonally similar to a finite section of the Feinberg--Zee hopping matrix, the theorem also determines the nilpotent tridiagonal sign matrices. We further show that the $(1,1)$ entry of the resolvent of a nilpotent $T_m(u)$ is $λ^{-1} \pm λ^{-3} \pm λ^{-7} \pm \dots \pm λ^{-(2^K - 1)}$, with signs that determine $u$. The proof of the main theorem has been formalised in Lean~4.

title: Proof Checking Continuous Reachability
abstract: This paper introduces a proof format and proof checker for certifying reachability computations of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) with polynomial vector fields. Establishing a proof checking framework for certifying ODE reachability is similar to the checking of UNSAT proofs for propositional satisfiability solving, but it is even more important due to the challenges inherent in dealing with ODEs, and even more challenging due to the numerical nature of ODE reachability algorithms. The proofs are expressed in differential dynamic logic (dL), and can be independently verified with symbolic theorem provers for dL (e.g. KeYmaeraX). Such proofs are naturally generated by reachability algorithms based on Taylor models, a popular technique to obtain rigorous bounds on approximations of ODEs. This paper proves the completeness of such proofs - if an approximation was correctly computed by some (possibly untrusted) reachability algorithm via Taylor models, then a corresponding proof in dL can be automatically generated and checked to be correct in dL's proof calculus. A dedicated proof checker is implemented in Lean4 for improved performance, which is capable of formally verifying benchmarks in the ARCH competition.

title: Linear dependence and tameness for homogeneous nilpotent-Jacobian maps in dimension four
abstract: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $H\in K[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]^4$ be homogeneous of positive degree. We prove that the components of $H$ are linearly dependent over $K$ whenever $JH$ is nilpotent, extending the known quadratic and cubic results to every positive homogeneous degree. This fills the gap regarding homogeneous linear dependence in four dimensions. The proof combines the nilpotent flag with the geometry of the geometric generic affine fibers and the projective image surface. Line fibers are treated by homogeneous quasi-translations. For nonlinear fibers, three successive invariants constrain the directions at infinity, reducing the nonplanar image to a developable surface or a smooth quadric. Boundary, ruling, and trace identities exclude both alternatives. We further prove that $X+H$ is one-stably tame in every degree and tame in four variables through degree five.
comments: 32pages, all theorems and proofs have been formally verified in Lean 4

title: Intent-Defined Radio: A Goal-Native Architecture for Next-Generation Wireless Networks
abstract: Wireless systems are becoming harder to operate because service goals are increasingly expressed in outcome-oriented terms, while radio platforms still expose mainly low-level configurations and protocol-specific controls. This mismatch makes it difficult to translate latency, reliability, throughput, and continuity requirements into coherent radio behavior. This article argues for Intent-Defined Radio (IDR) as a new system abstraction for next-generation wireless networks. Rather than treating the radio stack as a fixed mechanism set to be manually engineered and then tuned, IDR connects explicit service goals to executable radio behavior within a constrained design space by leveraging the capacity of large language models (LLMs). We position IDR relative to programmable radio, intent-based networking, and learning-based protocol design. We also present two simulation studies using Intent2MAC to illustrate the design loop, demonstrating executable MAC synthesis and offline refinement guided by evaluation feedback. The results show improved service satisfaction at a throughput cost and improved remote-control performance when random contention is replaced by distributed urgency-based arbitration. We finally discuss the open challenges in intent specification, evidence, hardware execution, interoperability, and lifecycle cost, and outline a staged path toward deployment.
comments: 7 pages, 4 figures

title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank III: Lattice points of the Kozlov polytope
abstract: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators and $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r Eg_i$ a graded free $E$-module with $°g_i=d_i$. Part I of this series identified the convex hull of the Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, $M$ a proper monomial submodule, as the Kozlov polytope $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$, a Minkowski sum of shifted Kozlov simplices, and described its vertices at rank two, conjecturing its facets there; Part II counted the Hilbert functions. Here we study the lattice points of the polytope. We show that the Kozlov simplex $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$ is a lecture hall simplex and that every point of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ has a unique chained decomposition into points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$. Hence the lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$ are exactly the sums of shifted lattice points of $\mathrm{Koz}(n)$, the polytope has the integer decomposition property, every lattice point is a Hilbert function when $n\le 3$, and lattice-point counts and Ehrhart polynomials are products of transfer matrices of the kind used in Part II. We determine the codegree of every Kozlov polytope and show that none is Gorenstein for $n\ge 3$. Finally we compare discrete and continuous invariants: the number of Hilbert functions against the volume and the lattice-point count, where we prove Kupreyeva's observed limit for the fraction of lattice points that are $f$-vectors and extend it to every rank. We also compare the centroid and second moments of the Hilbert functions with those of the polytope.
comments: 63 pages, 11 figures. Parts I and II are arXiv:2609.23605 and arXiv:2610.14985. Much of the paper is formalised in Lean 4 with Mathlib (no sorry, no extra axioms; marks in the margin say which results). Lean files, code and run logs: https://gitlab.liu.se/jansn19/exterior-convex and DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24288404

title: Optimal Patrol Widths in the Infinite-Corridor Barrier-Guarding Game
abstract: A guard of speed at most one and capture radius $r$ patrols an infinite corridor. An intruder knows the patrol and can follow any path of speed at most $q$ from one end to the other. We determine where the maximum width permitted by straight wall runners can be guarded against all such paths. Write $W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ for the supremum over patrols with bounded longitudinal excursion and $F(q)=2r\sqrt{1+(3q^2+2q-1)^{-1}}$ for the wall ceiling on $1/3 < q < 1$. A four-leg bowtie attains $F(q)$ exactly for $q_a\le q < 1$, where $0.457892036651 < q_a < 0.457892036652$. For every $1/3 < q < q_a$ the supremum is strictly smaller. As $q$ approaches $q_a$ from below, $F(q)-W_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)$ is bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of $r(q_a-q)^2$. The lower estimate controls near-optimal patrols uniformly in their period. A rescaled bowtie gives the matching upper estimate. We also prove that periodic patrols give the same supremum as bounded-excursion patrols. For $q\ge1$ the one-way optimum is $r\sqrt{4+q^{-2}}$, a transverse sweep. This sweep is optimal against transit in both directions for $q\ge1/2$. At low speeds, $qW_{\mathrm{opt}}(q)/r$ tends to two, and an explicit ten-leg patrol guards width greater than $(2/q-1.235353)r$ throughout $0 < q\le1/40$. Rational spacetime and flux certificates give finite-speed bounds, including $6.944691333740r < W_{\mathrm{opt}}(1/4)\le8.10r$.
comments: 34 pages, 2 figures. Exact rational Python verifiers and a Lean 4 library for selected lemmas and finite certificates accompany the submission

title: The FrontierOR Challenge: Agentic Algorithm Design for Operations Research
abstract: Operations research (OR) relies on algorithms that experts tailor to each problem: a new routing, scheduling or network design problem can take weeks of specialist work before it is solved well at scale. Large language model (LLM) agents now write, test and improve code, but whether they can design algorithms that scale to realistic instances is open: in the FrontierOR benchmark's one-shot evaluation, the strongest model matches Gurobi, with an objective within 1% of Gurobi's and no slower, on only 39% of the large instances. The FrontierOR Challenge asks teams to build agentic workflows that design, test, and improve algorithms for many optimization problems at once. Stage 1 releases 60 of the benchmark's 180 audited problems, spanning six application categories and five formulation types, in weekly rounds of 15; Stage 2 introduces new problems outside the benchmark, with unseen instances. Two tracks are ranked separately: in the Main track we run the submitted algorithms in a network-isolated sandbox with open-source dependencies only; in the Self-hosted track teams solve the instances on their own machines, with any software, within a timed window. Every solution is checked for feasibility, and a feasible solution scores the ratio of its objective to a frozen known reference, averaged over hidden instances.

title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
abstract: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $Δ^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$. We show that \[ c_d^{\mathrm{top}}=c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}=\frac{(d+1)!}{(d+1)^{d+1}}. \] The second equality confirms a conjecture of Bukh, Matoušek, and Nivasch, who established the upper bound. The proof was found by GPT-6 Astra, following the directions of the author.

title: Paper2Lean: Agentic Autoformalization of Mathematical Research Papers at Scale
